title: WISDOM Project - XV. Giant molecular clouds in the central region of the barred spiral galaxy NGC 5806
question: What are the physical properties, dynamics, scaling relations, and lifetimes of individual giant molecular clouds in the central region of the barred spiral galaxy NGC 5806, and how are they influenced by the bar?

data.sensitivity: 0.86 mJy beam^-1 (0.85 K) per 2 km s^-1 channel (cube); 25 uJy beam^-1 (continuum)

evidence.quote: Throughout this paper, we adopt a distance $D=21.4$ Mpc for NGC 5806 (cite: cappellari2011), whereby $1\ensuremath{''}$ corresponds to $\approx103$ pc.

recipe.goal: Calibrate, combine, and image the ALMA 12CO(2-1) cube and continuum
recipe.method: Calibrate raw data with ALMA pipeline; manually weight C40-3 (0.2) and C40-6 (1.0), combine with ACA using concat; subtract continuum with uvcontsub; interactively clean with tclean to dirty cube RMS depth.
key_parameters: Briggs robust = 0.5, pixel size = 0.05'', channel width = 2 km s^-1, C40-3 weight = 0.2, C40-6 weight = 1.0

recipe.goal: Generate moment maps and define galactic regions
recipe.method: Smooth-moment masking method: convolve cube spatially with a Gaussian equal to synthesised beam width, Hanning-smooth spectrally, mask at 1.5x RMS of smoothed cube, apply to original cube; divide galaxy into four regions (nucleus, arcs, nodes, dust lanes).
key_parameters: Mask threshold = 1.5 x RMS of smoothed cube; nucleus = inner 250 pc

recipe.method: Use modified CPROPSTOO algorithm: generate 3D mask of islands (2 adjacent channels > 2.5 sigma_rms expanded to > 1.5 sigma_rms, area >= 2 beams), find local maxima in running 3x3x3 pix^3 sub-cubes, decompose into clouds across a stepped range of minarea and minpix.
key_parameters: minvchan = 2, Delta T_max = 2 sigma_rms = 1.7 K, minarea = 96 to 24 spaxels (step 24), minpix = 96 to 24 pixels (step 24), convexity = 0.5

recipe.goal: Calculate physical properties of identified GMCs and fit their distributions
recipe.method: Compute cloud size R_c, observed velocity dispersion sigma_obs,los, gradient-subtracted velocity dispersion sigma_gs,los, CO(2-1) luminosity, gas mass M_gas, and surface density Sigma_gas; fit Gaussian curves to property distributions and estimate uncertainties with 500 bootstrap samples.
assumptions: Distance D = 21.4 Mpc, geometric parameter eta = 1.91, line ratio R_21 = 1, X_CO = 2 x 10^20 cm^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1 (alpha_CO(2-1) = 4.4 M_sun (K km s^-1 pc^2)^-1), inclination i = 58 deg, PA = 166 deg

recipe.method: Fit cumulative gas mass distributions above the mass completeness limit with power-law and truncated power-law functions using the 'error in variable' method and bootstrapping.
key_parameters: M_comp = 2.4 x 10^5 M_sun, delta_M = 1.03 x 10^4 M_sun, RMS surface density sensitivity = 17.8 M_sun pc^-2, beam area = 565 pc^2; 5 most massive clouds excluded in nucleus and nodes regional fits

recipe.goal: Measure internal velocity gradients of individual clouds and compare with galaxy rotation and turbulence
recipe.method: Fit a 2D plane v_bar(x,y) = ax + by + c to the intensity-weighted first moment map of each resolved cloud using MPFIT2DFUN to derive projected angular velocity omega_obs and rotation axis PA phi_rot; compare with low-resolution galaxy velocity map model (omega_model, phi_model), Burkert & Bodenheimer (2000) turbulence relation, and sigma_gs,los.
assumptions: Solid-body rotation plane approximation; turbulence relation omega = 1.6 (R_c / 0.1 pc)^(-1/2) km s^-1 pc^-1

recipe.goal: Assess dynamical states, scaling relations, virial parameter, and X_CO variations
recipe.method: Fit power laws to size-linewidth (R_c vs sigma_obs,los), virial mass vs gas mass (M_obs,vir vs M_gas), and virial parameter vs velocity dispersion; analyze Sigma_gas vs sigma_obs,los R_c^(-1/2) pressure curves; infer X_CO distribution assuming virial equilibrium.
assumptions: Homogeneous spherical cloud shapes (b_s = 1/5); alpha_obs,los = 1 for inferring X_CO variations

recipe.goal: Estimate bar-driven gas inflow rate and compare inflow kinetic energy with turbulent dissipation in the nuclear ring
recipe.method: Measure average velocity difference between double peaks in node LOSVDs to obtain V_in = V_in,obs / sin(i); compute mass inflow rate M_dot_in = 2 <Sigma_gas> W_in V_in and kinetic energy input rate E_dot_in = 0.5 M_dot_in V_in^2; compare with turbulent energy dissipation rate E_dot_diss = M_NR sigma_NR^3 / (2 h_NR).
key_parameters: W_in = 100 pc, <Sigma_gas> = 200 M_sun pc^-2, i = 58 deg, M_NR = 2.2 x 10^8 M_sun, sigma_NR = 16 km s^-1, h_NR = 16 pc
assumptions: Inflow occurs in galaxy plane with inclination i = 58 deg; two dust lanes of width 100 pc

recipe.goal: Estimate GMC lifetimes and disruption timescales in the nuclear ring
recipe.method: Calculate travel time between nodes t_travel = pi R_NR / (V_c,NR - Omega_p R_NR); count clouds in adjacent azimuthal zones (N_I, N_II) to find lost fraction F_lost = (N_I - N_II)/N_I and lifetime t_lifetime = (t_travel / 2) / F_lost; compare with collision (t_coll), shear (t_shear), and turbulent crossing (t_cross) timescales.
key_parameters: R_NR = 320 pc, V_c,NR = 150 km s^-1, bar end = 3.5 kpc, corotation radius = 4.2 kpc, V_c(4.2 kpc) = 220 km s^-1, D_c = 78 pc, sigma_cc = 10 km s^-1, elliptical annulus (230 pc inner, 370 pc outer, ellipticity 0.3, 85 clouds), Oort's A = 0.15 km s^-1 pc^-1, R_c = 39 pc, sigma_obs,los = 7.4 km s^-1
assumptions: Pattern speed of nuclear ring equals large-scale bar pattern speed; corotation radius is 1.2 times bar length; cloud-cloud velocity dispersion sigma_cc = 10 km s^-1

score_reason: Raw ALMA project codes, CASA versions, visibility combination weights (0.2 and 1.0), imaging parameters (robust=0.5, pixel=0.05'', channel=2 km/s, RMS=0.86 mJy/beam), and CPROPSTOO parameters (SNR thresholds 2.5/1.5, minvchan=2, Delta T_max=1.7 K, minarea/minpix=96-24 step 24, convexity=0.5) are all explicitly specified. However, the modified CPROPSTOO code is not publicly linked, the region boundary coordinates are only shown graphically, and the rotation curve derivation is omitted.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA data are public under two stated project codes, the data reduction and cloud decomposition parameters are thoroughly documented, and the paper provides a rich set of quantitative answer keys (cloud catalog, property distributions, scaling relation slopes, mass function slopes, inflow rate, and cloud lifetimes).
